name: Credit card or debit card abuse (unauthorized use or presentation)
officialTitle: CREDIT CARD OR DEBIT CARD ABUSE.
conduct: With intent to obtain a benefit fraudulently, presenting or using a credit or debit card knowing that it was not issued to the actor and is being used without the cardholder’s effective consent. Card and cardholder have the definitions in (a); covered card numbers or descriptions can qualify without production of the physical card. Effective consent and benefit retain their statutory meanings.
penalty: State jail felony: ordinarily 180 days to two years in a state jail and a possible fine up to $10,000. If the offense was committed against a person age 65 or older, §32.31(d) makes it a third-degree felony, ordinarily two to ten years in prison and a possible $10,000 fine. Qualifying prior convictions or findings can change punishment; the ordinary range is not a prediction for an individual case.

name: Credit card or debit card abuse (expired, revoked or cancelled card)
officialTitle: CREDIT CARD OR DEBIT CARD ABUSE.
conduct: With intent to obtain a benefit fraudulently, presenting or using a credit or debit card knowing it has expired or has been revoked or cancelled. Subsection (c) creates notice-based presumptions of knowledge and receipt of notice, not automatic guilt. Card and cardholder have the definitions in (a); covered card numbers or descriptions can qualify without production of the physical card. Effective consent and benefit retain their statutory meanings.

Card and cardholder have the definitions in (a); covered card numbers or descriptions can qualify without production of the physical card. name: Fraudulent use or possession of identifying information (another person, fewer than five items)
officialTitle: FRAUDULENT USE OR POSSESSION OF IDENTIFYING INFORMATION.
conduct: With intent to harm or defraud another, obtaining, possessing, transferring or using identifying information of another person without that person’s consent or effective consent. This choice requires fewer than five items of identifying information. Items are not automatically the number of documents or people: name and date of birth are combined in (a)(1)(A), not two separate items. Other identifying data may identify alone or in combination. The three-person intent presumption in (b-1) is separate from item-count grading and is subject to (b-2)’s lawful business/government exception. A presumption does not replace all offense elements.
penalty: State jail felony: ordinarily 180 days to two years in a state jail and a possible fine up to $10,000. If proved at trial that the offense was against an elderly individual (age 65 or older), or that identifying information was fraudulently used with intent to facilitate a registration offense under article 62.102, (c-1) raises the grade one category: Third-degree felony: ordinarily two to ten years in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. Court-ordered restitution may include lost income and other resulting expenses, excluding attorney fees. Qualifying prior convictions or findings can change punishment; the ordinary range is not a prediction for an individual case.

name: Fraudulent use or possession of credit card or debit card information (fewer than five items)
officialTitle: FRAUDULENT USE OR POSSESSION OF CREDIT CARD OR DEBIT CARD INFORMATION.
conduct: With intent to harm or defraud another, obtaining, possessing, transferring or using a counterfeit credit/debit card, the number and expiration date of a credit/debit card without account-holder consent, or digital-imprint data without account-holder consent. Counterfeit includes the specific false-issuer, altered-imprint, inconsistent-account-data and altered-card forms in (a)(1), not any card merely suspected to be invalid. This choice requires fewer than five items under §32.315(e). The five-item rebuttable presumption concerns lack of consent for (b)(2)/(3), not intent and not counterfeit cards under (b)(1); lawful business/government activities have the (d) exception. It is not the three-person presumption in §32.51.
penalty: State jail felony: ordinarily 180 days to two years in a state jail and a possible fine up to $10,000. Court-ordered restitution may include lost income and other resulting expenses, excluding attorney fees. Section 32.315 does not supply §32.51’s elderly/registration one-category enhancement. Qualifying prior convictions or findings can change punishment; the ordinary range is not a prediction for an individual case.
